checks.name: Field completeness
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test release field_completeness && grep -n 'pub fn from_canonical_bytes' rust/crates/automonique-protocol/src/release.rs
checks.output: The 'enforced at parse' clause now has a parse step to exercise. `ReleaseManifest::from_canonical_bytes(&[u8]) -> Result<Self, ManifestError>` exists at release.rs:739 and reads the document with `crate::wire::parse_canonical`; grep for 'fn parse|fn from_str|serde|json' inside release.rs finds no second JSON parser and wire.rs is unmodified in this candidate (git diff --stat lists exactly two files: src/release.rs and tests/release.rs). Measured through the PARSE path, on canonical documents built with JsonValue::to_canonical_bytes so the fixtures are canonical by construction: the required-field table has 9 entries and deleting each key from a complete document is refused naming exactly that field - schema_revision, version, source_revision, build_target, protocol, events, database_schema, sdk, and digests naming 'binary_digest'. The test asserts the table length is 9, so a silent shrink fails. A `digests` map that is present but carries only a policy entry gives the same MissingField{field: "binary_digest"}, so the required artifact and not merely the section is enforced. An empty document `{}` fails with MissingField{field: "schema_revision"} rather than producing defaults. Coverage of the declared field set is now mechanical rather than restated: the test classifies 9 required plus 3 optional keys and asserts that sorted set equals the parser's own public KNOWN_MANIFEST_FIELDS ([&str; 12]), so adding or removing an interpreted key without updating the table fails the test; each of the 3 optional keys (capabilities, credentials, rollback) is then shown to be absent-tolerant AND retained when present (evaluate_capabilities returns Refused{missing_required: ["cgroup_v2"]}, credentials()[0].name() == "database", rollback().version() == "0.0.9"). Bounds apply on the way in: an empty version, a version with U+0007, and a 200-byte source_revision are refused through the document with category field_invalid, the last one exactly as Field{field: "source_revision", error: TooLong{max_bytes: 128, actual_bytes: 200}}. Wrong JSON types are refused naming the field, 10 cases, all FieldType{field}: schema_revision as a string, schema_revision as -1, version as an integer, build_target as null, protocol as an integer, sdk as a string, digests as an array, capabilities and credentials as objects, rollback as an integer. Non-document input is refused as a document: `{"schema_revision": 1}` (one space) is Document{error: NonCanonicalJson} rather than normalized, `{` is Document{error: MalformedJson}, `{}5` is Document{error: TrailingData}, and a top-level `5` is FieldType{field: "manifest"}. Retention is bounded: 65 unknown fields give TooManyUnknownFields{max: 64} through both the builder and the parse path, and exactly 64 are accepted and retained. The parse path and the builder are proven to be one validation, not two: a complete document parses to a value that compares equal (assert_eq! on ReleaseManifest) to the manifest the builder assembles from the same data. Command output: field_completeness 10 passed / 0 failed; whole file 43 passed / 0 failed (was 23).

checks.name: Schema revision
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test release schema_revision
checks.output: Builder path unchanged and still measured: a builder declaring MAX_SUPPORTED_MANIFEST_SCHEMA + 1 = 2 and supplying no other field fails with UnsupportedSchemaRevision{supported_max: 1, declared: 2}, not MissingField. Parse path added and measured twice. Weak case: a document containing only {"schema_revision":2} yields UnsupportedSchemaRevision{supported_max: 1, declared: 2}, so no missing field takes precedence. Sharp case, which is what actually pins the ordering: an otherwise complete document with schema_revision 2 AND `version` as the integer 1 also yields UnsupportedSchemaRevision, because the revision is read and compared before any other field is decoded; a reader that decoded first would answer FieldType{field: "version"} (verified - see the negative control M-C1, which produced exactly that). Unknown fields within a supported revision are retained and never reinterpreted: through the builder, two string-valued unknown fields keep their supplied order and values; through the document, an unknown key holding {"depth":2,"names":["a","b"]} is retained as that exact JsonValue - not flattened, not stringified, not promoted into a known field - and the manifest's own version() still reads 0.1.0. Retained unknown values are JsonValue rather than text, so preservation is exact for any JSON shape. 5 passed / 0 failed.

checks.name: Range algebra
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test release range_algebra
checks.output: VersionRange::new(6, 4) fails at construction. Four overlap cases resolve as declared through negotiate_protocol, which returns a typed MajorVersion or a typed ManifestError rather than a boolean: overlapping 1..=4 against 3..=7 yields 4, identical 1..=4 yields 4, touching-at-one-version 1..=4 against 4..=9 yields 4, and disjoint 1..=4 against 6..=9 yields category range_invalid whose rendering contains both operands, '1..=4' and '6..=9'. New: the same algebra is now enforced on the parse path. A document declaring protocol {"min":6,"max":4} is refused with Range{field: "protocol", error: InvertedVersionRange{min: 6, max: 4}} - the decoder does not reorder it, which negative control M-D2 confirms is a real check. A document declaring events {"min":0,"max":4} is refused with category range_invalid and field "events_min", so the refusal names the offending bound and not merely the range. The 'empty ranges fail at construction' clause still has nothing to observe: MajorVersion wraps NonZeroU32 and the range is inclusive, so an empty range is unrepresentable rather than refused. That is a stronger property than the row asks for, but it is a limit on what this row measured, not a pass on it. 3 passed / 0 failed.

checks.name: Digest discipline
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test release digest_discipline
checks.output: Constructor path: six algorithm spellings are refused with UnacceptableDigestAlgorithm - md5, sha-1, sha1, crc32, the empty string, and the uppercase SHA-256. Only sha-256 and sha-512 are accepted, with hex lengths 64 and 128 enforced; a 4-character sha-256 digest fails with MalformedDigest{expected_len: 64, actual_len: 4} and an uppercase 64-character hex string fails with malformed_digest, so digests have one spelling. Decode path added, which is what the row's 'at parse' wording actually requires: the same six spellings are refused when they arrive in a manifest document, both as the binary artifact digest and as the SDK schema digest - twelve parse refusals, all UnacceptableDigestAlgorithm, all through DigestAlgorithm::from_wire. A document declaring sha-512 with 64 hex characters is refused MalformedDigest{expected_len: 128, actual_len: 64}; one declaring sha-512 with 128 characters parses and reports algorithm() == Sha512. ArtifactKind gained the matching decode path: from_wire round-trips all six defined spellings, returns None for 'kernel' and for 'Binary', and a document naming a 'kernel' digest is refused UnknownEnumValue{field: "digests"} rather than being silently dropped or coerced (negative control M-D1 opened the enum and the test failed). A mismatch yields DigestMismatch{artifact: SchemaBundle}, whose rendering contains 'schema_bundle' and neither digest body. Digests of different algorithms never compare equal. Constant-timeness is established by reading ArtifactDigest::matches, not by a timing measurement, and that limit is restated here deliberately: the compare loop XOR-accumulates every byte pair into one accumulator and returns only after the loop, with the sole early returns on algorithm inequality and length inequality, both of which are public properties. No timing experiment was run and the repository test could not have detected a data-dependent early exit. 6 passed / 0 failed.

checks.name: Rollback coexistence
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test release rollback_coexistence
checks.output: A release with database schema range 4..=6 and a rollback target declaring 1..=2 is refused by build() itself with RollbackIncompatible{release_min: 4, release_max: 6, rollback_min: 1, rollback_max: 2}, so the refusal happens in the manifest layer before any handoff decision exists. The identical refusal is now measured through the parse path: a document whose rollback section declares database_schema 1..=2 against the release's 4..=6 is refused with the same typed value, so a manifest document cannot smuggle in an incoherent rollback target. An overlapping target (3..=5 against 4..=6) builds and the target version is retained, by both routes. A manifest with no rollback target builds and reports rollback() == None, by both routes; negative control M-E2 invented a default target when the section was absent and the test failed, so that assertion is real. 4 passed / 0 failed.

checks.name: Capability requirements
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test release capability_requirements
checks.output: Against two required capabilities (cgroup_v2, landlock_abi_3) and one optional (systemd_adapter): a host offering all three yields CapabilityOutcome::Satisfied; a host missing only the optional yields Degraded{missing_optional: ["systemd_adapter"]}; a host missing a required one yields Refused{missing_required: ["landlock_abi_3"], missing_optional: []}; and a host missing one of each yields Refused carrying both lists separately, with an explicit assertion that the outcome does not match Degraded. Refusal and degradation are distinct enum variants rather than a boolean plus a list, so a reader cannot collapse them. New: the required/optional distinction survives the parse path and has no default. A parsed document declaring cgroup_v2 required and systemd_adapter optional degrades, not refuses, when only cgroup_v2 is offered. A capability entry that omits `required` is refused MissingField{field: "capability_required"}, and one declaring it as the string "yes" is refused FieldType{field: "capability_required"} - it is never assumed optional (negative control M-D3 defaulted it to optional and the test failed). 5 passed / 0 failed.

checks.name: SDK compatibility
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test release sdk_compatibility
checks.output: SdkCompatibility carries the SDK protocol range and the schema digest the SDK was generated against, and admits() answers from those two fields alone with no SDK loaded. Measured on a built manifest: protocol 1 and 2 with the declared schema digest are admitted; protocol 3 with the correct digest is refused (range 1..=2); protocol 1 with a different digest is refused. The same three answers are now measured on a manifest that came from a document, with the parsed range asserted equal to 1..=2 and the parsed digest equal to the declared one, so both a protocol-range mismatch and a schema-digest mismatch are detectable from a parsed manifest alone. Negative control M-E3 discarded the decoded SDK range and pinned it to 1..=1; the parse-path test failed, so it is measuring the decoded value rather than a coincidence. 2 passed / 0 failed.

checks.name: Secret hygiene
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test release secret_hygiene
checks.output: The live defect is fixed at the cause. The absolute-host-path rule no longer lives at the build_target call site; it lives in a new bounded-string type, ManifestText, whose inner value is private and whose only constructor validates non-empty, <= MAX_MANIFEST_FIELD_BYTES, control-character-free and not-an-absolute-host-path. Every manifest string field is now that type: ReleaseManifest.version, .source_revision, .build_target, CredentialDescriptor.name, CapabilityRequirement.id, RollbackTarget.version and both halves of a retained unknown field. Measured, builder/constructor side, as an 8-entry table whose length is asserted: version, source_revision, build_target, unknown_field_key, unknown_field_value, credential_name, capability_id and rollback_version each refuse '/etc/automonique/secret.pem' with AbsolutePath{field: <that field>}; CapabilityRequirement::optional refuses it too. That is all 7 fields the earlier probe found, plus capability_id, which that probe did not test. Measured again, parse side, as the same 8-entry table driven through manifest documents: all 8 refuse with the same typed error. Nesting is not a hole: an absolute path three levels inside a retained unknown value is refused AbsolutePath{field: "unknown_field_value"}, and an absolute path used as a nested object KEY is refused AbsolutePath{field: "unknown_field_key"}. Spellings measured as refused: '/etc/automonique/secret.pem', '/', '/opt/automonique/bin', '\\\\server\\share', '\\etc\\automonique', 'C:\\Windows\\System32', 'c:/windows'. Measured as accepted: 'x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu', '0.1.0', 'etc/automonique/secret.pem', 'C:relative', '~/.config/automonique', and a 40-character git revision. A field added later cannot opt out: the rule is keyed on the type, not the field name, so ManifestText::new(ABSOLUTE, "a_field_added_next_year") is refused AbsolutePath{field: "a_field_added_next_year"}, and the private inner value means there is no second way to build one - verified standalone with rustc, not only by the doctest harness: compiling `ManifestText { value: "/etc/automonique/secret.pem".to_owned() }` against the built rlib produces error[E0451] 'field `value` of struct `ManifestText` is private', while the paired program that differs only in going through ManifestText::new compiles, runs, and prints the AbsolutePath refusal. The credential half is unchanged and still passes: CredentialDescriptor::new takes (name, version) only, and compiling `CredentialDescriptor::new("database", 3, "s3cret")` against the built rlib produces error[E0061] 'this function takes 2 arguments but 3 arguments were supplied'; that compile_fail doctest now also carries a paired passing example that differs only in dropping the third argument. No error rendering contains the synthetic secret, either digest body, or the rejected path itself - asserted over seven refusals including two from the parse path. 8 passed / 0 failed. Negative controls: deleting the rule from ManifestText::new failed 7 secret_hygiene tests; restoring the pre-fix arrangement (the rule applied only when field == "build_target") failed 6 of them while the old single-field test `an_absolute_host_path_is_refused` still PASSED - which is exactly why the row was previously recorded as passing when it was not.

extra_checks.name: No I/O and no real artifact hashed
extra_checks.output: The release test binary runs 43 tests and issues zero network syscalls (the trace file is 0 bytes). release.rs references no std::fs, std::net, std::process, SystemTime, and no hashing crate; the only grep hit for the pattern is the substring inside 'ArtifactDigest::new'. ArtifactDigest stores a validated hex string and never computes one, so no real artifact is hashed in this slice, and the new parse path reads bytes handed to it rather than opening anything. Every digest in the tests is a synthetic 64- or 128-character literal.

extra_checks.name: Refusal category table
extra_checks.output: ManifestError now declares 13 categories: malformed_document, unsupported_schema_revision, missing_field, field_type, field_invalid, range_invalid, unknown_enum_value, unacceptable_digest_algorithm, malformed_digest, digest_mismatch, rollback_incompatible, absolute_path, too_many_unknown_fields. Three are new with the parse path (malformed_document, field_type, unknown_enum_value). All 13 are now reached by the repository suite; too_many_unknown_fields, which the previous audit recorded as unexercised, is reached by a new test that supplies 65 unknown fields through both the builder and a document and also proves exactly 64 are accepted. The ValueError::ZeroBound path remains unreachable from this module: MAX_MANIFEST_FIELD_BYTES is a non-zero constant and release.rs no longer calls a bound-taking helper, so no input can produce it.

notes: Base 4b491316751b2e489e10d6d5b495dbab7948612e is this worktree's HEAD, verified with git rev-parse. Toolchain: cargo 1.93.1, rustc 1.93.1. All nine contract rows are now measured and passing; the three that were open are closed as follows. (1) Field completeness was unmeasured because the crate had no decoder; it now has ReleaseManifest::from_canonical_bytes, built on crate::wire::parse_canonical - no second JSON parser, and wire.rs was not edited - and each of the nine omissions is refused naming its field through that path. (2) Secret hygiene was a live defect: six of seven bounded fields accepted an absolute host path. The fix moves the rule into a new ManifestText type with a private field and a validating constructor, so the eight bounded fields all refuse and a field added later cannot forget. (3) Quality failed only on automonique-lab suites that were red at the old base; re-measured here the workspace is 1052/0. Limits deliberately left in the record rather than smoothed over: the absolute-path judgement is syntactic and offline (leading '/', leading '\', or a drive-letter prefix) and does NOT refuse a '~'-relative spelling such as '~/.config/automonique' - that is tested as accepted, so the behaviour is pinned rather than accidental, but a reviewer who reads 'no absolute host path' as covering home-relative spellings would call it incomplete; constant-time digest comparison is still established by reading the compare loop, not by any timing experiment; an empty version range is unrepresentable rather than refused at construction; and ValueError::ZeroBound is unreachable from this module. One deliberate strictness worth naming: a string anywhere inside a retained unknown field must satisfy the full ManifestText rules, so a future manifest carrying an empty string inside an unknown field would be refused. That is consistent with the crate's refuse-rather-than-normalize discipline and is documented on from_canonical_bytes, but it is a real constraint on forward compatibility and is recorded here rather than hidden. Two API shapes changed inside this item's own lease and no other crate uses them (grep shows only ArtifactDigest is imported elsewhere): ReleaseManifest::unknown_fields() now returns &[(ManifestText, JsonValue)] instead of &[(String, String)], which makes retention exact for any JSON shape, and the AbsolutePath refusal renders as 'must not be an absolute host path' rather than 'must be a relative path' now that it covers UNC and drive-letter spellings. Nothing outside rust/crates/automonique-protocol/src/release.rs and rust/crates/automonique-protocol/tests/release.rs was modified.
